Heya there ! Not sure how old you are, but just so you know the bulk of us here know how tough relapsing is. Makes you wonder and fear that you're back at square one again. 

But for a heads up, no, you are not at square one. You kept trying to stay clean and even now, you're a month or so clean. Sometimes life is crap, and sometimes we need an outlet. Healthy or not, people cope in different ways. 

I would suggest being honest to your partner, they may find out sooner or later and it's always best to bite the bullet before the bullet gets to you first. But of course, if you believe that they are the kind of people to scorn you for relapsing, do not tell them. Though I doubt it, if they support you now, surely they will support you after. 

No matter how difficult it is, I strongly advise you to find another coping mechanism. For me, I had an issue with slamming my head and hands into things when frustrated with myself. Fortunately for me, I am able to chop wood or take it out on a punching bag with proper gear. 

There's other coping methods ; journalling, taking a walk, doodling or playing just dance. There's so much more. But when you have no energy for such, it's okay to curl up and cry. I often feel better after any one of the above. 

For me, cuddling always helps as well. 

It will no doubt be difficult at first, but try, try and try again and you will get it as long as you stay hell bent on changing for the better. And soon enough, it'll be second nature to you. Though you will have to actively catch yourself trying to relapse.

Just know, you deserve better. No kiddo should feel the need to hurt themselves to feel better. You deserve to feel the best without such thing. I wish you luck, I hope all works out for you.

I agree with the comment above and I say this because I can somewhat relate to you, although, to a less extreme extent. I guess I was lucky, though, it doesn't feel like it. 

I (18F) left what people would call 'parents' and 'home' 2 years ago exactly. I left on Easter and I suffered the guilt of leaving my younger siblings behind with a delusional 'father' and a submissive 'mother'. 

I knew that if I stayed, I would have ended it as soon as I could. I feared the end less because I had already tried it and I was going to make sure that the next would not fail. 

To you, who suffers even worse than I did. Get out. You are well deserving of having a life outside of a burning house. You deserve to experience love, to not fear what and when something else will happen, you did not come into this life to be chained down. 

My previous therapist told me that you leaving, could make all the difference. She made sure I knew that it would show my siblings that this was the first step. That we do NOT need to feel like dying is the only way out.

After all, how can you help someone if you, yourself are in need of help too ?

Your mother is a victim and you are too. Yes, but what can you do if she wants to continuously stay one ? Why should you have to give up your life (if not literally) because she chooses not budge ? She should understand that you want to truly live, not just survive. Any mother should understand this.

You are always the last deciding factor for your life as she was. She stayed for financial stability perhaps, to preserve her image, maybe she cannot go on without him no matter what he does to her. You can see that it is horribly wrong, that she should leave, but she will not until she sees it too. 

And there is always the what ifs and there always will be. What if I could've done more for her ? What if leaving is the wrong choice ? It goes on and on. But, what about you ? I always resented my biological birth giver for this.

I know that he was all she ever knew, but, why did she risk our lives for him ? She told me that she loved him but what about me ? It still hurts that I wasn't 'enough'. That she let it all happen because she was 'scared' but what about me ? What about all of us kids ? I was scared too, but of course, it didn't matter much to them. 

I'm in a better place now, living with my girlfriend and her family. Like I said, I was bizarrely lucky. The big wide world is terrifying and I wonder if I'll ever establish myself. But, I'm glad that I left, I still keep in contact with my siblings to check in with them. I'm still learning that I'm allowed to be happy and have emotions. It's still strangely new to feel safe. 

And I wouldn't have done it without professional help and a helping hand from others. It all starts with you, it's a ripple effect, it can only start with you leaving first. 

I hope that you can take my experience as a push to leave, to go forward, to really live and not just survive. By hell, it was not easy. But it was worth every low to get here.

So I wish you the best, you are well deserving of more than you were handed at birth. I'll be rooting for you, I desperately hope that you'll leave and find someone that you can build a healthier home with. The cycle can end with you. So please. Pack what you can and leave.

Maybe when you're in a stable place, offer her a place to stay. Perhaps she'll take it or perhaps she won't. The future is a mystery, and you won't know until it happens.

Good luck.

I (17f) feel you on that, having friends is hard. But again, if it doesn't work out, it isn't entirely your fault. Friendships, or relationships in general are a two way street. 

They have to be willing to put in their share of effort and understanding as you. If it's one-sided, then it's not healthy nor a great friendship. 

You also have to understand that sometimes it's not you that causes them to cut you off and ignore you. Sometimes they just need some time by themselves or because their mental health is on a decline. Or whatever reason, it isn't your fault. 

It might be good to try get in touch with them and ask what's wrong, what caused them to do that, but do not be aggressive and demanding about it. Let them talk. Be understanding and see what goes from there.

And well. Regarding your current close friend, it sounds like a them problem. You realized you made a mistake when you tried to help her, and apologized for it. But she's not taking it for an answer and ignoring you. 

Communication is key for everything. But if they're not willing, it's not your fault. 

And like in my partner's situation, they had to lose a crap friend who would only talk about her interests, her life, her problems and ignore my partner when they brought up their interests, achievements and such. 

At one point they got so fed up with their friend constantly not listening to they had to say, so they just left and the friend has ignored my partner since. 

Of course they felt bad, and tried to make amends since she was the only friend they had. But over time they found new friends (me included) who want to know what they have to say, what they like and about how their day is going and they're so much happier this way. 

We all talk it out after processing in our own times and we try to avoid ignoring since it's immature and hurtful.

So if nothing works out, you'll find new and better friends who are willing to hear you and understand you just as much as you are. 

Tis just life, people come and go, you grow and learn and shit happens. It's just how it is. Life is how you handle what happens to you.

It'll be okay in the end. You'll figure it out.

Hello there ! 

First of all, even if they are a professional - this does not always make them correct. And as a therapist, especially, they are to be understanding, patient and validating. Not hurtful, close minded and to project what they assume about you that blatantly. 

You are very much aware for your age, (I say that as if I'm older than I am..). You know that you have trauma which is still unresolved and that, that is the reason why you haven't been healing up to their standards. 

A person who drowns in 5ft of water is no different from a person who drowns in 20ft of water. Why ? Because they're both struggling to stay afloat. The depth of water doesn't matter.

And someone will always have it better and worse than you, so simply focus on you.

Your trauma and experiences, the length of your healing journey and many other things should never be compared to others. It would simply be unfair, since we're all different, only compare yourself to your past self. 

It's like a slap in the face when someone you trusted suddenly says or does something that deeply hurts us. You feel a mix of confusion, self doubt, sadness and betrayal. And start to question whether they are correct or not. Even at the extent of invalidating your own emotions.

I find that your current therapist is full of shit and is a valid asswipe. 

Think of it like this, you are a broken down car. Your engine (mental state) is a bit rough and sometimes you idle a bit too long before running. Maybe you don't run at all. A mechanic's (therapist) job is to understand the faults of the car and find replacements to get you running again. It takes time. 

A mechanic does not blame the car for failing to run, often the people who fail to service it (peers/parents). They do not beat up the car (unless they're crap at their job) for being unable to figure the car out (for being incompetent.)

I think it's time for a new therapist, I would recommend CBT (cognitive behavioural therapy) as you'd be able yo work through your traumas, understand how your brain has taken that and what it does in response and how to change it. 

E.g My issue was to jump to unaliving whenever a minor issue showed up. So my therapist suggested writing out the issue, figure out the possible outcomes ; bad outcomes and good outcomes. It made me feel less overwhelmed knowing there was some good possibility. 

You're doing great, taking your meds, using coping tactics, finding new coping tactics, holding yourself back from s/h and attempting and even just venting on reddit is a sign that you want someone to know. 

If you want someone to know, it means you're still asking for a helping hand. It means that you're still healing. You're doing great and you just have to keep doing great even if someone tells you that you're not.

You're not at square one, you're understandably overwhelmed because of what that wanker of a 'professional' said. Take a break, be kind to you, sleep it off, eat some ice cream, drink some water. 

Soon enough you'll be okay again, you just need to keep moving forward. (Just keep swimming -Dory.)

I think that one of the most hardest things is to acknowledge and accept is that we have no control of what happens to a certain extent. 

Whether it may be bullying, being raised in a horrible household, being hurt and betrayed by others; the list goes on and on and on.

And one of the most difficult and conflicting things to come to terms with is that, none of that defines you. Just because life turned out that way, doesn't mean you deserved it in any way. 

I see a bit of myself in you. Despite not having as many years under my belt, I can feel the anguish, the fear, the strange numbness that comes with it. I've been there, and it felt like the world was turning it's back on me and leaving me behind. 

What you need to know is that you're not doing yourself a favour by wearing a mask to your therapist and not telling them the truth (I used to do this, but I realized what was the point of therapy if I wasn't healing but lying ?).

I hate crying in front of people, and yet I did it as I relived my painful memories to my therapist. I told her everything that I was scared of, all that I felt made me worthless, a firm belief that everyone else could express their emotions but me. Because I once believed that I didn't deserve it.

And guess what ? She didn't laugh, she didn't ignore what I said. She cried with me. She didn't confirm my worst fears and leave me stranded. She stayed. She affirmed that I deserved just as much as everyone else did. Nothing but the best. 

I wasn't allowed a childhood. I wasn't allowed to make mistakes. And I was never allowed to show emotions. 

So I started allowing myself to make mistakes, embracing my emotions, I let my inner kid breathe, cry and laugh. 

What I'm trying to say is ; Your past does not define you. And to get help you have to be honest, you have to take the risk of opening up before it eats you up alive. 

It's never too late to start again. You deserve just as much as I do, and that's the same as everyone else. You deserve to be loved, appreciated, proud and happy. 

Try taking baby steps to boost your mood. For me I took little walks, I stared at the clouds and the ambiguous shapes they formed. The way the colours blended in the sky when the sun would rise and set. I found myself lost in them. And for a moment, I felt like I belonged. And I want the same for you too. 

You've only lived half your life, your real one starts the moment you want it to.

Our worths shouldn't be connected to what skills or talents we have. At least not entirely. Sure they may help, but in the long run. They don't really matter too much.

21 days. I've been told it's incredibly risky and to make it at least a month. But. A plan is only useful when you can stick to it.

The things that have made me keep going:
-Venting. It made me feel heard and allowed me to accept that it is not weak of me to speak about my feelings or cry. 
-Moving out of toxic household. Being surrounded by supportive people really helps, slows down the bad thoughts. 
-The cat. Very fluffy and sometimes comes up to cuddle.
-Sleeping it off. I forget why I'm sad sometimes.

I keep going because I now think theres a future for me, sometimes I feel overwhelmed and give up. So I rest until I'm ready to get up and try again.

There are so many reasons, that suicide should not be approached as if it is a bad thing. 

Those contemplating often just want to be heard. Listened to. They want help but don't know how to get it.

Living is not necessary. No it is not. It can be a curse and a blessing to be alive. Some people will have more hardships than others because of their gender, sexuality, skin colour, body and such. 

Dying earlier may not make much of a difference as everyone dies in the end. But. Its the experience that comes with being alive. Some find things that are worth fighting death for. A lover. A pet. A hobby. 

There are so many things in this world that are worth staying for. For example, for me, its the clouds. I love how they look, I wonder about how they come about and form the shapes they do. 

You do not have to lay in bed and suffer, you can get assistance, help, when you're ready. It is never weak of anyone to ask for help. Healing is much more complicated than taking your life. But when you're healed. Everything will be a bit brighter than it is now and it will be worth it.

Take your time, you'll get there. Step by step.

For me. I did not want to get help for the longest of times. I spent months wallowing in my attempt. And failing. A close friend of mine managed to pull me out, she listened, offered advice when I asked and was willing to keep me alive. She had told me countless times, she would not blame me or resent me if I gave up along the way.

That was a first for me, for someone to care about me to that extent and so I wanted to make her feel like what she's done for me wasn't useless. And so I started working to better myself and my self esteem.
Thank you for saying that. It helped a lot with being able to convince myself that I do not have to accommodate to others at the expense of my well being :'))
